newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks end up with modest gains.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks end up with modest gains.

text.p: * Index fails to sustain initial break through 3,200 resistance
Philippine shares rose for the second straight day, helped by secondliners, traders said.

"The rise in the main index was supported by secondary issues with most of the blue chips unchanged or declining, that's why we saw some slight pullback late in the session," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Citisecurities Inc.
At close of trade, the main index recovered and was 9.10 points higher, or up 0.29 percent, at 3,195.47 points.
Irving Ackerman, president, I. Ackerman & Co, said secondliner food stocks were picked up by investors on the expected recovery in the food sector this year.
Gainers beat losers 69 to 59 with 47 issues unchanged. But value turnover at 1.9 billion pesos was still below average.
Caesar Tanquingcen, trader at Connell Securities Inc, said the market would continue its gradual and steady rise on Wednesday on continued optimism on the Philippine economy.
He said the index will attempt to test the 3,200 resistance which it briefly broke through in early trade today.
